coordinates.locator: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim record of way 340213340, CERN - Point 1 (ATLAS) (reused anchor, about 480 m from the tunnel; it does not itself describe TI12)
coordinates.note: No CERN geodetic or survey publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the FASER/TI12 tunnel location was found (home.cern and the INSPIRE experiment record state only the distance and direction from ATLAS IP1, not coordinates; a Nominatim/OpenStreetMap search for the tunnel name returned only generic CERN-campus results). FASER is stated to be 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point in the unused service tunnel TI12 (INSPIRE experiment record, corroborated independently by home.cern/science/experiments/faser). As a placeholder, this record reuses the coordinate value already used for ATLAS Point 1 (46.2355606, 6.0546968), the nearest existing CERN point, since the detector is only about 480 m from it, well inside the stated precision. It is a campus-grade point with large uncertainty, not a surveyed hall position.

name: TI12 tunnel (FASER)
notes: TI12 is a former LEP-era transfer tunnel, 480 m downstream of ATLAS interaction point 1, reused to house the FASER detector.
The coordinate is a reused neighbouring-point placeholder (campus-grade, large uncertainty); see the coordinate note.

summary.plain: An unused service tunnel at CERN, 480 metres from the ATLAS collision point, that now holds the FASER experiment, searching for rare particles thrown straight down the beamline.
summary.technical: TI12, a former LEP transfer tunnel 480 m downstream of LHC interaction point 1 along the beam collision axis; houses the FASER detector, installed during Long Shutdown 2 (2019-2021).
